introduced.evidence: Contract goes to a coordinator-chosen --contract file, not a parent directory; distinct per worker.
Missing --contract triggers a usage line, but every command in scope gains --contract, so no command lacks a place to write its contract.
Every 3.1 command (cleanup-audit, init-lite, index-repo, brainstorm) is assigned contract work in P1 and no contract path is named for a command that never writes one.
brainstorm and init-lite are assigned to P1 and are briefed with the flags only from that phase.
No worker_status field; step 4 and WC-5 read status from the --contract file.

The --contract file is refused if it already exists, while WC-3 lets the worker re-invoke the command after the blocked contract was written, with no rule that the re-invocation takes a new --contract path (only coordinator retries get one in WC-6/2.3). Refusal text: "if the file already exists it prints one usage line and writes nothing" (L52); re-invoke text: "then re-invoke or resume the command with the answer as a flag" (L62).
Coordinator answers via a retry Task (--retry-of) with a new --contract path, not an unrelated Task.
